text.p: German tyre manufacturer Continental AG said on Tuesday it posted higher sales and profit for the first three months of 1997 and expected a "significantly pleasing" profit for the year.
Continental said first quarter pre-tax earnings rose to 88 million marks ($51.7 million) compared with 75 million marks in the 1996 quarter with a 1.4 percent rise in sales to 2.52 billion marks.

The Hanover-based group said at its annual news conference that it expected to post about a five percent growth in sales to about 11 billion marks for 1997 but did not make a projection on potential growth in profit.
"We hope for a significantly pleasing increase in profits in 1997," Continental chief executive Hubertus von Gruenberg said in the text of a speech at the news conference.
"As in 1996, the sources of earnings growth can be found in our many new high-tech products as well as internal productivity-enhancing and cost-curbing efforts," he said.

Von Gruenberg said Continental expected in particular for "clear earnings growth" from its Continental General Tire as well as its ContiTech, its technical products division, and its passenger tire business in 1997.
He based the outlook on prospects for moderate economic growth during the year but did not want to make a concrete projection on the potential earnings growth.
Continential in 1996 reported an increase in net income to 192.5 million marks, up 24 percent from 155.2 million marks in 1995. Sales rose 1.7 percent to 10.43 billion marks.

Von Gruenberg said he expected ContiTech to "undoubtedly break through" the three billion mark sales level for the first time in 1997 after achieving a 6.2 percent gain in sales to 2.97 billion marks in 1996.
He said Continental's product line has "made a fine shift" toward high-tech sophistication, helping to improve earnings along with efforts at enhancing production processes.
